audit.note: all three button presses ROUND-TRIP and the backend answers with follow_up_action( control_global, BUSY_INDICATOR show/hide ) plus cs_event-start_timer - the global BusyIndicator reproduced 1:1. Corrected 2026-08-21: the note still described the pre-rework MESSAGE_TOAST substitution, which the port's own deviation says is gone.

deviations.what: Since 2026-07-30 the global sap.ui.core.BusyIndicator behaviour is reproduced 1:1: each button fires a backend event whose response chains follow_up_action( control_global BUSY_INDICATOR show [delay] ) with the original's delay (default / 0 / 2000) plus follow_up_action( start_timer HIDE_BUSY duration ) (4000 / 4000 / 1000); the HIDE_BUSY timer round-trip then issues BUSY_INDICATOR hide - the frontend-action form of showBusyIndicator(iDuration, iDelay) + setTimeout(hideBusyIndicator). START_TIMER's single-slot semantics (a new timer replaces the pending one) match the original's clearTimeout of _sTimeoutId. Timing nuance: the hide fires after duration + one round-trip latency, and the show after the press round-trip - a few ms later than the original's purely client-side call; the press attributes are rewired from the controller handler names to backend events (the earlier MessageToast substitution is gone).

the BUSY_INDICATOR show/hide chain and the START_TIMER HIDE_BUSY round-trips are unverified in a running system - verify the overlay appears (default and zero delay), disappears after ~4s, and never appears in the 2s-delay/1s-duration case. **e2e-verified 2026-07-30, sharpened 2026-08-23** (transpiled-framework interaction, scripts/e2e-smoke.mjs): the module used to assert only that the overlay appears after the click and is gone later, which the FRAMEWORK satisfies on its own - View1.controller.js shows the same global singleton on every request and hides it in the finally of _processAfterRendering, before the port's follow-up JS runs at all. It now measures how long the overlay stays up and requires an episode of at least 2s: the framework's own episode ends when rendering finishes, so only the port's show(0) + START_TIMER( HIDE_BUSY, 4000 ) can produce one. The default-delay and 2s-delay/1s-duration buttons are the identical wire with different literals and stay unasserted.
